newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan urges caution on regulating derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan urges caution on regulating derivatives.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Friday that the need for government regulation of derivatives and the markets they trade on should be re-examined to make sure the rules are useful.
Speaking to a Florida conference sponsored by the Atlanta Fed bank, he said Congressional efforts to reform regulation of derivatives under the Commodity Exchange Act have raised contentious issues.
In some cases, there is no need to apply government regulation because the parties involved already were managing risks effectively, the Fed chairman suggested.

"The application of the Commodity Exchange Act to off-exchange transactions between institutions seems wholly unnecessary -- private market regulation appears to be achieving public policy objectives quite effectively and efficiently," Greenspan said.
A text of his remarks was issued in Washington.

Greenspan said a move toward centralized trading or clearing of financial derivatives that now are bilaterally negotiated and cleared "should not be obstructed" by threatening to apply the Commodity Exchange Act to them.

The Fed chairman said alternatives to bringing regulation of clearing systems for such markets under the Commodity Exchange Act should be made available and suggested banking regulatory agencies or the Securities and Exchange Commission could do the job.
Greenspan suggested futures exchanges should be given more scope to offer clearing services.
"... Subject to a few restrictions, futures exchanges should be allowed to create affiliates to compete as providers of such services," Greenspan said.
